name: DX-Ball
listSummary: In-progress DX-Ball reconstruction using REA and Ghidra; original game files required.
summary: From a classic brick-breaker to readable C/C++. Follow a reconstruction workflow that compares recovered functions against the original executable.
evidenceScope: The project README describes Codex using REA with Ghidra to inspect and recover functions. The official REA showcase demonstrates the sound-pan calculation.
limitation: Original game files are required. A matching function is not proof of whole-game equivalence; we have not built or played this project.

name: VSL-DSP
listSummary: AudioBox VSL research and Linux tools, with REA contributing focused DSP findings.
summary: An open-source hardware project with Linux device detection and DSP parameter tools. REA findings inform a specific part of its vendor-protocol research.
evidenceScope: The README credits LazyOwn's REA integration and Ghidra for recent vendor-library and DSP findings, not the entire pre-existing driver project.
limitation: Not a verified replacement for Universal Control. The README identifies hardware fault injection as remaining work for bulk I/O. We have not tested a device.
licenseNote: Kernel detector sources declare GPL-2.0-or-later; consult the per-file notices.

name: Notion clipboard bridge
listSummary: REA case study of Notion's clipboard pipeline, not a replacement app.
summary: Trace a copy operation from the page through preload scripts and IPC to the system clipboard, then examine how rich block data stays connected.
evidenceScope: The official case study shows REA findings for Notion's tab preload, followed by reading the wrappers and receiver in the packaged application.
limitation: This is not an open-source Notion replacement. No standalone alternative repository is linked by the case study; it is a focused investigation, not a complete app rebuild.

name: TH04 bullet-ring reconstruction
listSummary: Focused REA study of TH04's bullet-ring behavior within a broader reconstruction.
summary: See how a ring of bullets turns toward the player. A documented REA inspection connects 16-bit instructions with a readable angle calculation.
evidenceScope: REA's official showcase verifies a focused bullet-ring inspection. The linked repository is a broader game reconstruction; the evidence does not attribute that whole project to REA.
limitation: Full-game validation has separate open work. The repository requires your own legal game copy; its source license does not cover original game assets.

name: OpenBattlefield2
listSummary: Incomplete Refractor 2 reimplementation with REA investigation tooling; original game required.
summary: An in-progress reimplementation of the Refractor 2 engine. Its repository includes a REA helper for investigating user-supplied game binaries.
evidenceScope: tools/rea.sh explicitly invokes rea-agents with Ghidra and per-binary snapshots. Tooling presence does not establish that REA produced every engine subsystem.
limitation: Requires your own Battlefield 2 installation. The checked README lists missing firing, vehicle control and sound. Not a complete free replacement for the game.

name: GunZRs
listSummary: Rust game port with a separate REA investigation framework; original assets required.
summary: A Rust game port that reads assets from the user's Steam installation, with a separate REA and Ghidra investigation framework in the repository.
evidenceScope: The README documents a target-independent REA framework. It also says game formats were recovered from data files; this does not prove the entire port was made with REA.
limitation: Requires your own game installation. We have not run it or checked retail feature parity. Included research tools are not an endorsement of every project claim.

name: OpenBSD netcat study
listSummary: Static REA and Ghidra analysis of an OpenBSD netcat binary.
summary: An author-published static investigation of a Linux netcat binary, with REA evidence files, Ghidra findings and cross-checks against standard binary tools.
evidenceScope: The repository names REA 6.2.0 and Ghidra 12.1.4 and links its raw analysis artifacts. Its reported findings are static, not a runtime test.
limitation: The target is already open source. This is a research write-up, not a new netcat implementation or proof that a binary is safe.

name: Aegis authenticator study
listSummary: REA case study tracing code generation in the existing Aegis Android app.
summary: Follow the methods behind a six-digit login code in a released APK, and see how the time-step rule explains why the code changes every 30 seconds.
evidenceScope: The official REA showcase traces code-generation methods in an Aegis release APK. It is an explanation of an existing open-source application.
limitation: Not a new authenticator, credential-recovery tool or account bypass. The study does not claim to recover another person's login codes.

name: DownUnderCTF flag checker
listSummary: REA walkthrough of a DownUnderCTF reverse-engineering challenge.
summary: A competition-style reverse-engineering example: follow checking functions, translate their constraints into equations and check a solution.
evidenceScope: REA's official showcase documents a DownUnderCTF flag-checker investigation and reports checking the solved result with the challenge program.
limitation: An educational challenge, not a commercial-software alternative. We reviewed the published account and did not rerun the challenge.

name: REA — Reverse Engineer Anything
listSummary: Upstream CLI and MCP toolkit for agent-assisted software analysis.
summary: The upstream toolkit connecting coding agents to binary, application and runtime investigations through MCP and a command-line interface.
evidenceScope: The upstream README documents rea-agents setup, supported targets, analysis providers and evidence-carrying workflows. This is the original project, not an unofficial mirror.
limitation: Provider and platform requirements vary. Local analysis does not mean the coding agent's model provider receives no data. Check current upstream requirements.

name: dsh-mcp-rea
listSummary: Community MCP bridge exposing a smaller selection of REA tools.
summary: A thin MCP bridge exposing a curated REA tool selection plus a CLI escape hatch for hosts that cannot filter a large tool catalog.
evidenceScope: The README documents the REA CLI invocation, selected MCP tools and local bundle integration. It is an adapter around REA, not a replacement analysis engine.
limitation: Requires REA and any necessary provider. The README warns its PATH fallback uses a shell; review the explicit REA_ENTRY mode. We did not execute or security-audit it.

name: REA Investigator
listSummary: Agent skill for planning, tracing, verifying and reporting REA investigations.
summary: An agent skill that organizes REA investigations into planning, tracing, verification and reporting, with a local evidence ledger.
evidenceScope: The README explicitly identifies the upstream REA CLI as its analysis instrument and documents modality routing and evidence-hash checks.
limitation: A structured workflow is not a guarantee that an agent's conclusions are correct. Claimed tests and agent compatibility are author-reported, not independently reproduced here.

name: rea-jev
listSummary: REA plugin with Jev-based evidence checks; external model calls and fail-open hooks.
summary: A community plugin pairing REA's MCP server with Jev-based routing, tool-call checks and evidence tracking around an agent investigation.
evidenceScope: The README documents the bundled REA MCP configuration, investigation skill, hooks and version pin. This is an independently authored integration.
limitation: Hooks fail open on provider failure. Jev may send excerpts to an external model service and incur charges; thresholds are not a security boundary. We did not install it.

name: rea-agents Homebrew formula
listSummary: Community Homebrew formula for the upstream rea-agents package.
summary: A community-maintained Homebrew formula for the rea-agents package, hosted in moonfruit's broader tap.
evidenceScope: Formula/rea-agents.rb points to the upstream REA homepage and npm package. Only this formula is listed, not every package in the tap.
limitation: Not an official REA distribution. Inspect the pinned formula and download provenance before installing; formula and packaged software have separate licenses.

name: rea-playbook
listSummary: Hands-on Electron lab with REA exercises and a separate offline demo.
summary: A runnable teaching project with a small Electron target, line-referenced evidence extraction, an MCP probe and a reconstruction exercise.
evidenceScope: The README names the published rea-agents package, explains its real-analysis path and distinguishes that path from an offline fixture-only demo.
limitation: The offline demo does not run REA. The no-native-engine claim applies to the JavaScript/Electron path, not arbitrary native binaries. Test claims were not rerun here.

name: rea-lab
listSummary: Windows/Ghidra setup, practice challenges and ongoing REA evaluation work.
summary: A Windows-focused REA lab documenting provider setup, isolated MCP registration, seeded challenges and work toward reproducible evaluation.
evidenceScope: The README names REA and Ghidra, links Windows verification contributions and separates completed environment work from benchmarks and planned features.
limitation: The live evidence pane is planned, not delivered. Verification and benchmark claims are author-reported. Targets are limited to authorized exercises and locally built binaries.

name: REA French community guide
listSummary: Unofficial French guide to REA concepts, setup and investigation workflows.
summary: An independent French introduction to REA, with setup guidance, an investigation walkthrough, provider explanations and responsible-use context.
evidenceScope: The repository explicitly identifies itself as an unofficial educational guide to morluto/rea and says it does not contain REA's own source code.
limitation: Educational documentation, not an analysis engine or official support channel. REA changes quickly; current upstream instructions take precedence over translated guidance.

name: Awesome AI Reverse Engineering
listSummary: AI reverse-engineering tool list featuring REA, in Chinese and English.
summary: A categorized list of AI reverse-engineering tools, including REA among agent, CLI and MCP-based investigation options.
evidenceScope: The list explicitly links morluto/rea in its agent-platform section. It is a discovery resource that features REA, not a collection of software built with REA.
limitation: This listing does not endorse every linked tool or transfer their test, safety or license claims. Check the individual upstream projects before use.

name: Awesome Reverse Engineering
listSummary: Broad reverse-engineering tool and learning list from REA's maintainer.
summary: A broad tools-and-learning list maintained by morluto, featuring REA alongside resources for binaries, apps, firmware, formats and protocols.
evidenceScope: The README features morluto/rea and describes its broader reverse-engineering scope. It is a companion resource list, not evidence that all listed tools use REA.
limitation: Individual listed projects retain their own licenses and requirements. Inclusion here is not an affiliation or endorsement of Awesome REA by the maintainer.

name: PhotoCraft
listSummary: Early-alpha Photoshop-style image editor in Rust; not yet a professional drop-in replacement.
summary: A Rust image editor recreating Photoshop-style workflows with layers, masks, typography and PSD documents.
evidenceScope: The upstream README explicitly targets Adobe Photoshop workflows and describes a separate Rust implementation. Source review does not establish clean-room legality or full behavioral parity; no REA involvement is claimed by this listing.
limitation: The author explicitly says it is not ready to replace Photoshop for daily professional work. AI features, tools, typography depth and plug-in compatibility remain incomplete. We have not installed, run or audited it.
licenseNote: The author offers MIT or Apache-2.0 at your option. Bundled assets have separate notices; ArtCraft names and logos are excluded from these code licenses and require rebranding in modified redistributions.

evidenceScope: The upstream README explicitly targets Adobe Illustrator workflows and describes a separate Rust implementation. Source review does not establish clean-room legality or full behavioral parity; no REA involvement is claimed by this listing.
limitation: Reliable native AI round-tripping, several effects, scripting and interaction fidelity remain incomplete. Affinity import is partial; Affinity export is not supported. We have not installed, run or audited it.
licenseNote: The author offers MIT or Apache-2.0 at your option. Bundled assets have separate notices; ArtCraft names and logos are excluded from these code licenses and require rebranding in modified redistributions.

licenseNote: The author offers MIT or Apache-2.0 at your option. Bundled assets have separate notices; ArtCraft names and logos are excluded from these code licenses and require rebranding in modified redistributions.

licenseNote: The author offers MIT or Apache-2.0 at your option. Bundled assets have separate notices; ArtCraft names and logos are excluded from these code licenses and require rebranding in modified redistributions.

evidenceScope: The upstream README explicitly targets Avid Pro Tools workflows and describes a separate Rust implementation. Source review does not establish clean-room legality or full behavioral parity; no REA involvement is claimed by this listing.

licenseNote: The author offers MIT or Apache-2.0 at your option. Bundled assets have separate notices; ArtCraft names and logos are excluded from these code licenses and require rebranding in modified redistributions.

licenseNote: The author offers MIT or Apache-2.0 at your option. Bundled assets have separate notices; ArtCraft names and logos are excluded from these code licenses and require rebranding in modified redistributions.

name: OpenRCT2

summary: An independent RollerCoaster Tycoon 2 engine reimplementation with modern-platform support and cooperative multiplayer.
evidenceScope: The upstream README documents a reimplementation of RCT2, supported builds and the requirement for original game data. REA use is not required or claimed.
limitation: Requires legally obtained RollerCoaster Tycoon 2 files. Its code license does not include the original game assets. We have not played it or verified feature parity.

name: OpenMW
listSummary: Morrowind engine and editor reimplementation; original game data required, mod compatibility varies.
summary: An independent Morrowind-compatible RPG engine and Construction Set replacement supporting the original game data.
evidenceScope: The upstream README describes the replacement engine and editor, reports completable main quests and documents mod-compatibility limits. The GitHub repository mirrors development hosted on public GitLab.
limitation: Requires ownership of Morrowind and its data. Some original-engine mods depend on quirks not reproduced here. Development-branch version numbers are not release guarantees; no gameplay test was performed.

name: OpenTTD
listSummary: Transport Tycoon Deluxe-style simulation with optional free graphics, sound and music.
summary: An open-source Transport Tycoon Deluxe reimplementation and transport simulation, with extensions and optional free graphics, sound and music.
evidenceScope: The upstream README says it aims to mimic and extend Transport Tycoon Deluxe, documents supported platforms and distinguishes free OpenGFX/OpenSFX/OpenMSX assets from optional original game data.
status: Released game; free asset sets available
limitation: Original graphics or music still require their own rights; free replacement asset sets have separate licenses. Add-ons and third-party components retain their terms. We have not run or benchmarked the game.

name: ScummVM
listSummary: Replacement engines for supported classic adventures and RPGs; original game data usually required.
target: Classic adventure and RPG game engines
summary: A collection of replacement game engines that runs supported classic adventures and RPGs using their existing data files.
evidenceScope: The upstream README explicitly says ScummVM replaces the original executable files while using the game data, and directs readers to per-game compatibility lists. It is not a bundled collection of commercial games.
limitation: Support and completeness differ by game and version. You normally need lawful game data, whose license is separate from the engine. Consult the official compatibility list; we did not execute any game.

name: Wine

summary: A Windows API compatibility layer and program loader for running Windows applications on supported Unix-like systems.
evidenceScope: The upstream README documents loading Windows executables and implementing Windows APIs through Unix, X11 or macOS equivalents. This is the Wine project mirror, not an entire replacement Windows installation.
limitation: Application compatibility varies and some programs can crash. Original applications retain their licenses. Use WineHQ for official releases and compatibility guidance; the mirror has no latest GitHub release, and we did not run it.

name: paper-rs
listSummary: Native Rust canvas modeled on Paper, with documented REA research; rendering and platform gaps remain.
target: Paper-style infinite canvas · Rust / egui / wgpu
summary: A local-first design and whiteboard app recreating Paper-style canvas behavior, with pages, vector editing, exports and an agent-facing MCP server.
evidenceScope: The README documents studying Paper Desktop with REA and implementing its behavior in Rust. The architecture writeup separates observed desktop-shell findings from inferred hosted-editor behavior; it does not establish full Paper parity.
limitation: No cloud collaboration or plug-ins. Rendering, text shaping and imports have gaps; macOS has only been type-checked by the author, not run on hardware. We have not built, run or audited it; clean-room claims are author-reported.
licenseNote: Bundled Inter fonts use SIL OFL 1.1. The author states that no Paper code or assets are included; the code license grants no rights to Paper's proprietary materials.

name: OpenGHub
listSummary: Linux G HUB-style peripheral manager using HID++ research; device support and firmware paths need care.
summary: A Linux-native G HUB-style manager for Logitech peripherals, implementing device settings, button assignments, lighting and profiles through HID++ and userspace services.
evidenceScope: The HID++ documentation explains recovering onboard-memory and macro formats from a real G502. The README and lighting notes describe G HUB settings imports, vendor-depot research and device-specific compatibility; no REA involvement is claimed.
limitation: Requires supported peripherals and Linux device permissions. Onboard macros flatten some behavior; firmware updates are not tested on every device family and can leave a device in its bootloader. We have not installed it or tested hardware.
licenseNote: Logitech artwork, firmware and databases are not covered by MIT or bundled as project assets. Some features import the user's G HUB data or fetch vendor files at runtime; their rights remain separate.

name: free-heroes4 (openh4)

licenseNote: No game data is included. Original game assets and third-party dependencies retain their own terms; the engine license does not grant rights to the commercial game.

name: Rook

licenseNote: Roblox places, models and client assets are not included or licensed by this repository. Dependency notices and permissions for user-supplied content remain separate.

name: OpenXcom

licenseNote: Bundled SDL_gfx-derived code is LGPL with author permission (per README).

licenseNote: README also contains conflicting “Public Domain” / non-commercial wording; LICENSE file is GPL-3.0. Original Carmageddon assets remain proprietary.

limitation: The README does not publish feature or parity status (roadmap is external). Requires original Sacrifice data, the LDC D compiler to build, and extra DLLs on Windows. We have not independently tested it.

name: ByroRedux
